extracted.intended_audience: PTAB judges, USPTO employees, and members of the public who nominate or interact with PTAB decisions
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and standards for nominating, reviewing, designating, and de-designating Patent Trial and Appeal Board decisions as 'Precedential' or 'Informative', including roles, quorums, conflict-of-interest rules, labeling, and publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default status of Board decisions (routine decision)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Board decision is, by default, a routine decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A routine decision is binding in the case in which it is made, even if it is not designated as precedential or informative, but it is not otherwise binding authority. The SOP provides a mechanism for highlighting certain Board decisions by designating them as precedential or informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may nominate a decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may nominate a routine decision of the Board for designation as precedential or informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Board members, other USPTO employees, and members of the public. Nominations should be submitted by email to PTAB_Decision_Nomination@uspto.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominations must set forth with particularity the reasons for the requested designation and identify any other Board decisions known to the nominator that may conflict with the nominated decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations that do not provide particularized reasons or that fail to identify potential conflicting decisions do not satisfy the stated nomination requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for precedential designation
rubrics_metrics.description: A precedential decision establishes binding authority concerning major policy or procedural issues, or other issues of exceptional importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include constitutional questions; important issues regarding statutes, rules, and regulations; important issues regarding binding or precedential case law; or issues of broad applicability to the Board. Precedential designation may also be used to resolve conflicts between Board decisions and promote certainty and consistency. An informative decision may be nominated for precedential designation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for informative designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An informative decision provides non-binding guidance and Board norms on recurring or novel issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for informative designation include: (1) providing Board norms on recurring issues; (2) providing non-binding guidance on issues of first impression to the Board; (3) providing non-binding guidance on Board rules and practices; and (4) providing non-binding guidance on issues that may develop through analysis of recurring issues in many cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory Committee composition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: An Advisory Committee of at least 11 members reviews nominated decisions and makes recommendations to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical members represent the Office of the Under Secretary (not including Director or Deputy), PTAB (not including members of the original panel for each case under review), Office of the Commissioner for Patents (not including the Commissioner or those involved in examination of the challenged patent), Office of the General Counsel, and Office of Policy and International Affairs. Meetings may proceed with less than all members; a quorum of seven members must be present. Additional individuals (technical experts or support staff) may participate but do not provide recommendations. The Committee prepares an advisory recommendation; if not unanimous, dissenting views are reported to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB Executive Management composition and role
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB Executive Management reviews nominated decisions and provides a recommendation to the Director on whether to designate a nominated decision (or portion) as precedential or informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For purposes of the SOP, PTAB Executive Management consists of the Chief Judge, Deputy Chief Judge, Vice Chief Judges, and Senior Lead Administrative Patent Judges (acting officers count). A quorum of five members must be present to make a recommendation; if a quorum cannot be reached, no recommendation will be provided. PTAB Executive Management will review the nominated decision and the Advisory Committee recommendation and, absent exceptional circumstances, will solicit feedback from Board members. If its recommendation is not unanimous, dissenting views will be reported to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board review period and solicitation of member comments
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB Executive Management will, absent exceptional circumstances, present the nominated decision to all Board members for comment during a Board review period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board review period typically will be five business days. During that period any Board member who does not have a conflict of interest with the nominated decision may submit written comments to PTAB Executive Management regarding designation. PTAB Executive Management may share those comments with all Board members, then compile and evaluate received comments and determine by majority vote whether to recommend designation. Summary of Board comments is included with the recommendation to the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest and recusal rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director, an Advisory Committee member, or a member of PTAB Executive Management has a conflict of interest, they must notify other members and recuse themselves from the designation or de-designation process for that decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO follows guidance set forth in the Standards of Ethical Conduct for Employees of the Executive Branch at 5 C.F.R. Part 2635 and will consult with the Department of Commerce Ethics Law and Programs Office as necessary. Conflicts may include involvement in the examination or prosecution of the underlying patent or a related patent. PTAB Executive Management judges will also follow conflict guidance in PTAB SOP 1 and will recuse themselves from discussion or analysis involving cases on which they are paneled. The Director will not consult with anyone having a conflict of interest with the designated decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of recommendations to the Director and Director authority
rubrics_metrics.description: PTAB Executive Management submits its recommendation, the Advisory Committee recommendation, and a summary of Board comments to the Director, who must approve any designation or de-designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may consult with others (e.g., Office of the General Counsel) and retains ultimate authority: no decision or portion thereof may be designated or de-designated pursuant to these procedures without the Director’s approval. The SOP does not limit the Director’s authority to designate or de-designate decisions or to issue policy directives at any time and in any manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of portions of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A decision, or a portion thereof, may be designated as precedential or informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If only a portion is designated, the label must indicate that portion. The designation label should include whether it is 'Precedential' or 'Informative' and the date of designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling, publication, and dissemination requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions or portions designated as Precedential or Informative must be labeled and published or disseminated appropriately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designated decisions shall be labeled 'Precedential' or 'Informative' and include the date of designation; posted electronically on the Board’s Precedential and Informative Decisions Web page and may be sent to commercial reporters that routinely publish Board decisions. Where designation would make a decision open to public inspection that otherwise is confidential under 35 U.S.C. § 122(a), publication or dissemination will follow notice and opportunity for written objection as afforded by 37 C.F.R. § 1.14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of designations
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal/operational effect of each designation type is specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A precedential decision is binding Board authority in subsequent matters involving similar facts or issues. An informative decision sets forth Board norms that should be followed in most cases, absent justification, but is not binding authority on the Board. A decision previously designated under a prior SOP remains designated unless de-designated under the SOP's de-designation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: De-designation process and permissible grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may suggest that a Board decision designated as 'Precedential' or 'Informative' should no longer be designated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons include the decision has been rendered obsolete by subsequent binding authority, is inconsistent with current policy, or is no longer relevant to Board jurisprudence. Nominations for de-designation should be submitted to PTAB_Decision_Nomination@uspto.gov. If the Director determines a decision should no longer be designated, the decision will be de-designated, the Chief Judge will notify the Board, the decision will be removed from the Precedential and Informative Decisions Web page, and the public will be notified.
